claims.text: DFT-based simulations of oxide formation can predict oxidation resistance in metallic materials under high-temperature conditions.
DFT-based simulations of oxide formation can be used to enhance oxidation resistance in metallic materials.
The proposed method applies to crystalline metallic materials.
The relevant oxidation conditions are above 500°C in an oxygen-rich environment.
Oxide-layer formation is the structural mediator linking the proposed method to oxidation resistance.
DFT can provide thermodynamic analysis of oxide growth.
DFT can provide kinetic analysis of oxide growth.
DFT-guided oxide modeling will produce a 20% increase in oxidation resistance relative to the baseline.
Increased oxidation resistance can be measured as a decrease in oxide-layer thickness.
The proposed method is applicable over 500–1000°C.
The proposed method is applicable at oxygen partial pressures of 0.1–1 atm.
The accuracy of the DFT simulations may be limited by the choice of exchange-correlation functional.
The complexity of oxide formation may limit the accuracy of the DFT simulations.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome defines improvement as a 20% decrease in oxide-layer thickness, whereas the falsification rule refers to an oxide-layer thickness increase of less than 10%. The direction and threshold of the test do not correspond to the stated prediction.
